sources.entry: dill - Extends pickle to serialize almost any object, including closures and interpreter sessions.

summary.one_liner: dill is a Python library that extends pickle to serialize almost any Python object, including lambdas, closures, classes, and whole interpreter sessions.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a pickle-compatible interface (dumps/loads, or "import dill as pickle") for converting Python objects to byte strings and back. It handles many standard types, exotic types such as nested functions, lambdas, code objects, cells, and method descriptors, plus classes, dataclasses, and metaclasses. It can save and restore an entire interpreter session in one command. It also offers source extraction via dill.source.getsource and a pickling trace tool in dill.detect for debugging serialization errors. Options such as byref, recurse, fmode, and protocol control how objects are serialized.
use_cases: send Python objects across a network as bytes
serialize lambdas or closures for multiprocessing
save and restore an interpreter session
extract source code from functions and classes
pickle objects that standard pickle cannot handle
notable: Drop-in replacement for the pickle module with the same interface
Saves and loads whole interpreter sessions
Serializes lambdas, nested functions, and closures that plain pickle rejects
Built-in pickle tracing (dill.detect.trace) for diagnosing failures
Part of the pathos heterogeneous computing framework
caveats: Not secure against maliciously constructed data; only unpickle trusted sources
Cannot yet pickle frames, generators, or tracebacks
Optional diagnostic tools and Windows session-history support need extra installs
